question_text: If y = sin⁻¹(2x/(1 + x²)), find dy/dx.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the substitution and the double-angle identity it produces.

steps.label: Put x = tan θ and use sin 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ)
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the whole question. The 1 + x² in the denominator means the substitution x = tan θ. The expression 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) is the tangent form of sin 2θ, so the inverse sine cancels a double angle here, not a triple one.
steps.memory_tip: 2x/(1 + x²) is sin 2θ, 2x/(1 − x²) is tan 2θ and (1 − x²)/(1 + x²) is cos 2θ — all three under the same substitution x = tan θ.
lines: Put x = tan θ, so θ = Tan⁻¹x
Then 2x/(1 + x²) = 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) = sin 2θ   [double-angle identity]
Take θ in [−π/4, π/4], that is −1 ≤ x ≤ 1. Then 2θ lies in [−π/2, π/2], the principal range of Sin⁻¹, so

recall.must_convey: That x = tan θ is substituted and 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) = sin 2θ, so y = 2 Tan⁻¹x.

steps.why: The direct quotient-and-chain-rule route leaves √(1 − 4x²/(1 + x²)²), which only simplifies after clearing the fraction and factoring a perfect square. The substitution reaches 2 Tan⁻¹x in one line instead.
common_mistakes: Substituting x = sin θ, which does not match the 1 + x² denominator.
Reading 2x/(1 + x²) as tan 2θ, which is 2x/(1 − x²) and has a minus sign.
Omitting the range and writing y = 2 Tan⁻¹x for every x, when the sign is different for x > 1.

steps.label: Differentiate 2 Tan⁻¹x
steps.margin_note: Second mark. d/dx(Tan⁻¹x) = 1/(1 + x²), with no square root anywhere. The answer keeps the 2 that came from the double angle.
steps.memory_tip: Inverse tangent has 1 + x² and no root; inverse sine has √(1 − x²). The substitution decides which one the answer carries.

recall.must_convey: That d/dx(Tan⁻¹x) = 1/(1 + x²), so the answer is 2/(1 + x²).

steps.why: The final form has no square root, and that is the check that the substitution was the tangent one. A root in the answer means the working ended with an inverse sine instead of an inverse tangent.
common_mistakes: Writing 2/√(1 − x²), by finishing with the Sin⁻¹ derivative because the question opened with sin⁻¹.
Losing the factor 2 and answering 1/(1 + x²).

insider_note: 2x/(1 + x²) is sin2θ under x = tan θ, so y becomes 2Tan⁻¹x — note it is Tan⁻¹, not Sin⁻¹. The answer 2/(1 + x²) carries no square root at all.
